5. Opinion of the Judge : Accused found not guilty.
JUDGMENT

This is a charge sheet filed by the PSI of CCB, Bengaluru City against the accused for the offence punishable U/sec.51(1) (B) & 63 of Copy Right Act and sec. 420 of IPC.
02.

The brief facts of the prosecution case is that, the accused within the limits of Yeshwanthapur Police Station in the shop named 'Time Center Sales and Services', situated at 1 st Main Road, Near Bombay Dyeing, Yashawanthapura Bengaluru, The CW.1 got information that, the accused was manufacturing of spurious / counterfeit reputed companies watches i.e., Hublot, Rado, Tissot,
Ediace, Fossil and Armani without obtaining any permission from the reputed companies and were selling the duplicate watches to the public and cheated the companies and public at large and thus the accused has committed the above said offences.
03.

After filing of charge sheet, this court took cognizance for the offences punishable U/sec.51(1)
(B) & 63 of Copy Right Act and sec. 420 of IPC and issued summons to the accused.
Accordingly the accused appeared before the court through his counsel and enlarged on bail.

Later on, charge sheet copies and prosecution papers were furnished to the accused under Sec.207 of Cr.P.C.
04.
Heard both side on framing of charge, perused the prosecution papers.

As there are sufficient materials to frame the charge against the accused, the charges has been framed and the same were read over to him, but they denied the contents of charge and claimed for trial.
Hence the case was posted for prosecution evidence.
05. In furtherance of the charges leveled against the accused, the following points are arisen for my consideration.
POINTS 01.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, the accused within the limits of Yeshwanthapur Police Station in the shop named 'Time Center Sales and Services', situated at 1st Main Road, Near Bombay Dyeing, Yashawanthapura Bengaluru, The CW.1 got information that, the accused was manufacturing of spurious / counterfeit reputed companies watches i.e., Hublot, Rado,
Tissot, Ediace, Fossil and Armani without obtaining any permission from the reputed companies and were selling the duplicate watches to the public and cheated the companies and public at large Nagaraj, Asi vs Syed Nasir on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92344898/
2 and thus the accused has committed the above said offences punishable U/sec.51(1) (B) & 63 of Copy Right Act and sec. 420 of IPC.?
2.
What order or sentence?
06. To prove the case, the prosecution has examined in all 6 witnesses i.e., CW.8, 4, 7, 5, 2 & 3 as PW.1 to 6 and got marked 9 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.9.
The prosecution has also not secured the presence of CW.1 & 6 and their evidence are also dropped.
07. After completion of evidence of prosecution, the incriminating circumstances in the evidence of the prosecution is read over to the accused and statement under section 313 of Cr.P.C. recorded.
The accused has denied the incriminating circumstances as false and not chosen to lead his evidence.
08. Heard the arguments.

My findings on the above said points are as follows:-
Point No.1 : In the negative.
Point No.2: As per final order, for the following:
REASONS 09. Point No.1: It is the specific case of the prosecution that, the accused has selling the spurious /
counterfeit branded watches of Hublot, Rado, Tissot, Ediace, Fossil and Armani without obtaining any permission from the reputed companies and were selling to the public.
With that aspect, CW.1 register the complaint as per Ex.P.7.
Based on the same, CW.7 registered the crime and submitted the FIR.
Based on the same, CW.8 conducted the raid and panchanama in the presence of CW.2 to 5 and recorded their statements and ultimately submitted the charge sheet.

For that, all the prosecution witnesses supported the case of prosecution, but CW.1 being the complainant and CW.6 being the authorized person of the reputed / Manager of reputed companies remained absent.
Hence, they dropped for evidence.

10. It is pertinent to note here that, even PW.1 to 6 were supported the case of prosecution, but there are lots of contradictions in their respective chief examinations as well as cross examinations.

It is significant to note here that, CW.8 / PW.1 in his examination in chief has deposed that,

Further, PW.1 in his cross examination has deposed that, "...

But, CW.3 / PW.6 who being the another panch witness has deposed that, "...   8       

 
   

     
 

 

   


 
   
 



  
....", which clearly creates doubt about the case of prosecution.

CW.8 / PW.1 in his cross examination admitted that "...

Further, PW.6 being panch witness has denied that, he is not a regular panch witness, but in his further cross examination he has deposed that, "....

These contradictory evidences of PW.1 to 6 creates doubt about the case of prosecution.

Apart from this, the counsel for the accused relied upon the order passed by Hon'ble High Court of Judicature,
at Madras passed in Crl. OP.No.6357/2021 and Crl.M.P.No.4248 and 4249/2021, wherein para No.7, it is held that;
" para No.7:- ..... it is clear that, unless the infringement relates to original literary,
dramatic, musical and artistic works, Cinematograph films and sound recordings, the provisions of the Act are not applicable.

entities.text:
High Court of Judicature,
at Madras
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In the instant case, there are no such allegations, hence, the offences punishable U/Sec. 63 of the Copy Right Act, 1957 is not made.
Such being so, the above said order is aptly applicable to the present case on hand.
Therefore, the benefit of doubt in the case of the prosecution is to be extended to the accused.
Therefore, by extending the benefit of doubt in the case of the prosecution to the accused, this court answers the above Points No.1 in the Negative.
11. Point No.3:-

In view of the findings recorded to the above points, this court proceed to pass the following;
ORDER
By exercising powers conferred U/sec. 248(1) of Cr.P.C., the accused is acquitted for the offences punishable U/sec.51(B), 51(1) & 63 of Copy Right Act and sec. 420 of IPC.
The bail bond and surety bond of the accused shall continue in force for a period of 6 months.
The accused is set at liberty.
The property reported in PF No.66/2018 marked being watches are ordered to be destroyed as worthless after appeal period is over.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer and print out taken by her is verified and then pronounced by me in the open court on this the 9th day of October 2024.)
(Sri. Vinod Balnaik.)
IX Addl.Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru City.
